entries.meaning: Transliteration of Hebrew יְהֹוָה (yəhōwā), the Masoretic vocalization of the Biblical Hebrew יהוה (variously pronounced). The Masoretic vocalization is a so-called qere perpetuum, the deliberate insertion of the vowels of another word than the one represented by the consonant text, in this case אֲדֹנָי (“my lord”) ('Adonai'). Continuing earlier Iehoua.

entries.meaning: From Middle English Juliana, from Latin Iūliāna.
entries.note: A female given name from Latin, Latin feminine form of Julianus, derivative of Julius.

entries.meaning: A variant of Julian, Juliana or Julianne. Can also be interpreted as a combination of Julia + Ann.
entries.note: A female given name from Latin.

entries.meaning: Modern combination of Julie + Anna, perhaps sometimes intended as a form of Juliana.
entries.note: A female given name from Latin.

entries.meaning: A 19th/20th century variant of Juliana. Can also be interpreted as a combination of Julia + Anne.
entries.note: A female given name from Latin.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from French Julien.
entries.note: A male given name from French, equivalent to English Julian.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Italian Giulietta, diminutive of Giulia, from Latin Iūlia, feminine of Iūlius, a Roman family name. Cognate with French Juliette.
entries.note: A female given name from Latin.

entries.meaning: Rare non-standard spelling of Julius.
entries.note: A male given name.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Latin Iūlius, of uncertain origin, possibly from Ancient Greek ἴουλος (íoulos, “downy first beard hairs”), i.e. the young, or from Latin Jovilius (“devoted to Jove”). Doublet of Jules.
entries.note: A male given name from Latin.

entries.meaning: Patronymic surname from a short form of Julian + -son.
entries.note: A surname transferred from the given name.

entries.meaning: Clipping of Junior.
entries.note: A diminutive of the male given name Junior

entries.meaning: Short for junior.
entries.note: A male given name, or more often nickname, for a boy who is junior to someone else, especially someone with the same name, such as his father.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Japanese じゅんいち (Jun'ichi).
entries.note: A male given name from Japanese.

entries.meaning: From junior. The town in West Virginia was established on November 13, 1897, and named after Henry G. Davis Jr. (1871–1896), a son of United States Senator from West Virginia Henry G. Davis (1823–1916) who had been drowned at sea off the Atlantic Coast of South Africa while returning home on the steamship Munkesenton.
entries.note: A male given name, from a nickname for someone with the title Jr. (junior).

entries.meaning: Non-standard spelling of Junius
entries.note: A male given name from Latin.

entries.meaning: A topographic surname from juniper. In some cases matronymic from an equivalent of Jennifer influenced by folk etymology.
entries.note: A unisex given name from English. A female given name from English.

entries.meaning: Reduplication of Jun.
entries.note: A diminutive of the male given name Junior

entries.meaning: From Middle English Juno, from Latin Iūnō of uncertain origin. One hypothesis is derivation from Proto-Indo-European *dyúh₃onh₂- (“she of heavenly authority”), from *dyew- (“sky, heaven”) + *-Hō (“burden, authority”), reflecting her role as goddess of rulers.
entries.note: A female given name.

entries.meaning: From Latin Iūpiter (“father Jove”), from Proto-Italic *djous patēr (literally “sky father”) (cognate with Ancient Greek Ζεῦ πάτερ (Zeû páter, “father Zeus”)), from *djous (“day, sky”) + *patēr (“father”), from Proto-Indo-European *dyḗws (literally “the bright one”), from *dyew- (“to be bright, day sky”), and *ph₂tḗr (“father”). Doublet of Dyaus Pita.
entries.note: A unisex given name.

entries.meaning: Variant of Justin.
entries.note: A male given name.

entries.meaning: From justice
entries.note: A male or female given name from English from the abstract noun justice.
entries.origin: English from the abstract noun justice

entries.meaning: Name of early saints, Latin Iūstīnus, from Iūstus + -īnus, from iūstus (“just”).
entries.note: A male given name from Latin, popular in the English-speaking world since the 1970s.

entries.meaning: From French Justine, from Latin Iūstīna, name of early saints, feminine of Iūstīnus, derivative of Iūstus, from iūstus (“just”). The feminine equivalent of Justin.
entries.note: A female given name from Latin.

entries.meaning: From Latin iustitia (“Justice”). Doublet of justice.
entries.note: A female given name from Latin.

entries.meaning: Name of several early saints, from Latin iustus (“just”), from iūs + -tus.
entries.note: A male given name from Latin.

entries.meaning: From Latin Iuvenālis.
entries.note: A male given name from Latin.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Arabic
entries.note: A female given name from Arabic

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Sanskrit ज्योतिस् (jyotis, literally “light”).
entries.note: A male given name from Sanskrit.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Sanskrit ज्योति (jyoti).
entries.note: A female given name from Sanskrit used in India.

entries.meaning: From Sanskrit ज्योतिस् (jyotis).
entries.note: A female given name from India.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Sanskrit ज्योत्स्ना (jyotsnā, “moonlight”).
entries.note: A female given name from Sanskrit used commonly in India.
